- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥ 0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% relative to prior peak.
- When sentiment is negative (≤ 0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward by 1–2% to reflect risk-off bias.
- After sharp price spikes (e.g., >5% from prior 7-day high), model frequently overshoots; cap forecast at 10–15% below peak or use 3-day moving average to smooth.
- If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to correct; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% per sentiment drop.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day horizon; if forecast is >10% above 30-day moving average, reduce by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For sentiment-heavy periods (e.g., 3+ consecutive 1.00 values), model tends to overreact; apply dampening factor of 0.85 to forecast weights.
